general.title: Plan service work in Sprints.
general.description: Break tickets into 1-2 week sprints, set dates around maintenance windows, and keep on-call progress visible.

comic.title: Sprints are repeating on-call windows.
comic.description: A recurring window — weekly, fortnightly, or per maintenance window — used to track a chunk of service work is a Sprint.

general.title: Save queues for your service team. Create as many as you need
general.description: Queues are saved ticket filters that you use frequently. All your colleagues in a project can see everyone's queues and choose whichever suits their on-call needs best.

comic.title: Queues work atop ticket properties.
comic.description: You can create a queue from here with as many properties as filters as you see fit.

no_issues.title: Create a ticket and assign it to someone, even yourself
no_issues.description: Think of tickets as incidents, requests, problems, or changes. A ticket and its sub-tickets are usually time-based actionables assigned to members of your team. Your team creates, assigns, and resolves tickets to keep services running.

comic.title: Tickets are building blocks in service operations.
comic.description: Onboard a new identity provider, migrate a database, or handle a service outage are examples of tickets that likely have sub-tickets.

general.title: Group tickets into Tracks per service or program.
general.description: A track groups tickets under one service, platform, or program with its own deadline and progress. See how far you are from done.

comic.title: Tracks help group service work by ownership.
comic.description: A payments service track, an identity platform track, and a data warehouse track are good examples of this grouping.

general.title: Write a runbook, SOP, or postmortem. Get Galileo, Terraline's AI assistant, to help you get started
general.description: Articles are your service knowledge base. Write runbooks, SOPs, shift handovers, and postmortems, format them easily, embed tickets, lay them out using a library of components, and keep them in your service context. To make short work of any doc, invoke Galileo with a shortcut or the click of a button.
